source_caption:
Few films capture the complicated nature of love quite like Happy Together. Wong Kar-wai explores a relationship that’s caught between affection and resentment, where two people keep finding their way back to each other despite knowing how much they hurt one another. There’s something deeply sad about watching people hold on to a relationship that seems to be falling apart, simply because letting go is just as difficult.

Tony Leung and Leslie Cheung are both incredible, bringing so much vulnerability and emotional depth to their performances. Combined with Christopher Doyle’s beautiful cinematography and the film’s use of music, it’s an experience that feels as intimate as it is heartbreaking.
-
🎥: Happy Together (1997)
Dir. Wong Kar-wai

source_details.synopsis: Happy Together (Chinese: 春光乍洩) is a 1997 Hong Kong romantic drama film written and directed by Wong Kar-wai and starring Leslie Cheung and Tony Leung Chiu-wai as a turbulent gay couple. The English title is inspired by the Turtles' 1967 song, which is covered by Danny Chung on the soundtrack. The Chinese title (previously used for Michelangelo Antonioni's Blowup) is an idiomatic expression suggesting "the exposure of something intimate".
